articles.title: DHL Fastest Pit Stop Award 2026
articles.summary: Ferrari broke the Red Bull dominance to secure the Fastest Pit Stop title in 2025.
articles.body:
Ferrari broke the Red Bull dominance to secure the Fastest Pit Stop title in 2025.

Pit stops are possibly the most visual evidence of why Formula 1 racing is a team sport.

The DHL Fastest Pit Stop Award was established in 2015 to recognise outstanding teamwork and performance from the 'unsung heroes' who make a critically important contribution to the drivers' success on the track.

articles.title: Sainz: "Todos los pilotos hablan de lo difícil y complicado que será Madring"
articles.standfirst: Acabó 13º, muy por encima de su Williams y ya mira a la prueba de casa del próximo fin de semana
articles.summary: Acabó 13º, muy por encima de su Williams y ya mira a la prueba de casa del próximo fin de semana
articles.body: Carlos Sainz acabó la carrera de Monza como 13º, por delante de Lawson y de los dos Haas, en una carrera que no se recordará, pero donde estuvo en un nivel excelente, a pesar de un problema en la entrega de su motor que le hizo perder muchos puestos en las dos primeras vueltas. Carlos reconocía ente la prensa española que le daba verdadero valor a su actuación. "Ha sido una de esas decimoterceras posiciones que no saldrán y no brillarán, pero por mi parte y por el equipo la verdad es que hemos hecho entre todos una buena carrera, con un buen pit stop, buena estrategia y buena ejecución", resumía. Para Carlos fue una nueva experiencia en Monza, por esa facilidad con la que se adelantaba al principio. "Ha sido un poco raro en el inicio, pero cuando la carrera ya se ha estabilizado se ha convertido en algo más normal... Pero en las 5 o 10 primeras vueltas ha sido curioso", reconocía. Ahora toca pensar en Madring y esa sensación de que puede ser un trazado 'car killer' (destrozacoches): "Creo que lo de 'car killer es para los F3 de momento. Habrá que ver si es un 'car killer' de F1 o no. Lo que está claro es que es un circuito muy complicado, muy espectacular. Todos lo hemos dicho tras hacerlo en el simulador, que nos ha sorprendido lo complicado que es y lo difícil que será", confiesa. "Por lo tanto yo creo que por lo menos en esa parte será un circuito con carácter, con dificultad, no un circuito más que se añade al calendario porque sí. Luego, si es demasiado o si hay que cambiar alguna curva o algún piano o lo que sea, pues ya habrá tiempo con el paso de los años para ir mejorando", añadía. En cuanto a los nervios por correr en casa, Sainz reconoce que será especial. "Tengo ganas de que llegue el viernes, de subirme al coche porque creo que antes voy a tener muchos eventos promocionales, mucho marketing, atender a sponsors y a medios, que ya sabéis que es la parte del piloto que más cuesta. Pero incluso en eso, voy a intentar disfrutarla al máximo porque es la parte que me toca en casa y tengo que hacer un esfuerzo extra por mi país y por mi ciudad", cerraba con los medios españoles en Monza.

articles.title: Italian Grand Prix: Harry Benjamin's driver ratings as Kimi Antonelli wins for Mercedes at Monza
articles.summary: BBC Radio 5 Live F1 commentator Harry Benjamin rates how the drivers performed during the Italian Grand Prix.
articles.body:
Kimi Antonelli pulled off one of the fightbacks of the ages as he fought from 19th on the grid to win the Italian Grand Prix.

The 20-year-old's stunning victory came after he caught and passed his team-mate George Russell with three laps to go.

Russell, who had started second and battled for the lead with Antonelli earlier in the race before holding on to first until the closing stages, is now 66 points behind in the drivers' championship.

Meanwhile, it was a difficult day for Ferrari in front of the tifosi, with Charles Leclerc enduring a high-speed crash at the Parabolica early on while Lewis Hamilton was forced to settle for sixth.

Here are my ratings for how the drivers performed across the whole weekend in Monza.

What more could you ask for? Started 19th because of an engine penalty and sliced his way through the field to win his home Grand Prix. A trip through the gravel while hunting Russell was the only scare in an otherwise extraordinary drive.

Fastest in both FP2 and FP3, missed pole by just 0.060 seconds and led a huge chunk of the race. The strategy ultimately swung things Antonelli's way but Russell hardly put a foot wrong himself.

Another very strong Sunday after Red Bull struggled more over one lap. Briefly led the race and fought hard with both Mercedes drivers before bringing home a podium despite reporting problems with the rear of the car.

Qualifying ninth wasn't where Norris wanted to be as McLaren struggled with its brakes, but he recovered well on Sunday. Beat Piastri in their late fight to take fourth and continued his strong run of form.

The speed was clearly there with third in qualifying, but the penalty for impeding Lawson dropped him back on the grid. He fought forwards throughout the race but ultimately lost out to Norris late on.

A much better weekend than sixth place suggests. Quick throughout practice and almost identical to Leclerc in qualifying, before being forced into the gravel during their first lap fight and having to recover from outside the points.

One of the performances of the season on Saturday to put an Alpine in pole position on pure pace. He simply didn't have the race speed to keep the quicker cars behind on Sunday, but seventh still completed a superb weekend.

Another hugely impressive rookie weekend. Qualified in the top 10 and then converted it into eighth place, comfortably leading Racing Bulls home and once again showing he belongs at this level.

Excellent qualifying to put the Alpine eighth but overshadowed by Gasly. Even found himself running fourth after the red flag. A big trip through the gravel cost him heavily, but recovering all the way back to ninth salvaged a deserved points finish.

A much tougher weekend than Zandvoort, particularly with 17th in qualifying while Lindblad reached Q3. Recovered nicely to score the final point, although lining up incorrectly for the restart was an unnecessary blemish.

Missed Q3 by just one thousandth of a second and again had the edge over Audi team-mate Hulkenberg. Just missed out on the points on Sunday but there wasn't much wrong with his weekend.

Couldn't quite match Bortoleto in qualifying or the race. He remained in the fringes of the points fight but ultimately finished behind his team-mate in 12th.

Williams never looked particularly comfortable at Monza. Sainz at least made Q2 and brought the car home in 13th, but there was little opportunity to make an impact further up the order.

A difficult weekend to judge given the grid penalty and subsequent pit-lane start. His qualifying was also hurt when Piastri impeded him, so fighting back to 14th was a respectable effort on his second successive weekend at Red Bull.

Antonelli takes stunning Monza win from 19th on grid

Antonelli 'walks over water' for win that will go down in F1 folklore

Far too late for title fight priority - Hamilton

There were encouraging signs from Haas' major upgrade and Bearman looked strong on Friday. Twelfth in qualifying was solid but slipping to 15th on Sunday meant the promising pace didn't translate into points.

Always looked to be facing a difficult weekend without the same upgraded Ferrari power unit as Bearman. Qualified behind his team-mate and finished behind him too in a fairly anonymous race.

His qualifying was compromised by both an engine penalty and helping Sainz with a tow. Made a little progress from the back on Sunday but Williams simply didn't have enough pace for him to get much further.

Another difficult weekend for Cadillac, although Perez at least beat Bottas in the race. Started near the back and never really threatened to make meaningful progress.

Out-qualified Perez but slipped behind him during the Grand Prix and finished two laps down. Cadillac remained well off the midfield throughout the weekend.

Qualified last and there was little to suggest Aston Martin had the pace to achieve much more. A hydraulics problem eventually brought a miserable weekend to an early end.

Aston Martin's lack of performance made this almost impossible from the outset. Qualified 21st, started from the pit lane after power unit changes and eventually retired with car damage.

A weekend that promised so much after topping first practice unravelled almost immediately on Sunday. His opening lap battle with Hamilton was too aggressive and then he lost the Ferrari at Parabolica on lap two to bring his home race to a spectacular early end.

articles.title: Italian Grand Prix: Lewis Hamilton says it is 'far too late' to be given priority over Charles Leclerc at Ferrari
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton says it is "far too late" for Ferrari to give him priority over team-mate Charles Leclerc in the championship fight.
articles.body:
Lewis Hamilton says it is "far too late" for Ferrari to give him priority over team-mate Charles Leclerc in the championship fight, following a disappointing weekend at their home Italian Grand Prix.

The seven-time world champion, who started fourth and finished sixth, was pushed on to the grass by Leclerc on the opening lap, slipping him down to 10th, as the pair battled wheel-to-wheel at the exit of the first chicane.

Leclerc then suffered a high-speed crash at the Parabolica shortly after to leave Hamilton as Ferrari's only hope of a top-three finish.

Once the race restarted following the red-flag period caused by Leclerc's crash, Hamilton never fully rejoined the fight at the front, and with Mercedes securing a one-two finish at Monza, he has fallen further back in the championship fight.

The 41-year-old, who was level on points with second-placed Russell in the standings before Sunday's race, is now 10 behind his old Silver Arrows team-mate, and 76 points adrift of title leader and race winner Antonelli.

"I think from today, we've just lost so much ground to [Mercedes] on points," said Hamilton.

Antonelli takes stunning Monza win from 19th on grid

Antonelli extraordinary as Gasly has superb weekend - driver ratings

"It's far too late for those decisions to come. It's too late. All I can do is just try and turn up. I'll get up tomorrow morning and I'll give it my best."

He added: "It's never over until it's over. I don't know how many points it is now, but I'm sure it's 60, 70. It's an amount that, with the pace that they have, it's a very, very difficult amount to close out."

Ferrari were left answering similar questions about who should take priority following the team's performance at the Dutch Grand Prix last month.

Hamilton, who is two places higher than Leclerc in the championship, was left frustrated in Zandvoort, as he felt the team took too long to move Leclerc - who was third and on a differernt strategy - out of the way so he could challenge for a podium, as he was on fresher tyres and quicker.

When they eventually did pit Leclerc, Hamilton responded over team radio: "Great way of wasting time, good job". He later apologised for his comments.

But the first-lap incident between the pair in Italy seems to have only intensified Hamilton's concerns.

Speaking after his lap-two crash, Leclerc said "it was way too close into turn one" between himself and Hamilton. He added that he was unaware whether the pair had made contact.

"I was quite a lot on the inside kerb and tried to make the corner, which I didn't do it tight enough," said Leclerc.

"And then I only saw in the mirrors what happened, which is never what you want between two cars of the same team."

However, Hamilton said: "I was ahead in turn two by the ethics, I was ahead. There was no 'we' in it."

When asked if Ferrari fans should be worried the dynamics between himself and Leclerc may turn into a team-mate feud, he said: "Look, I don't race dirty. I've always raced clean and fairly and always left space. So I don't think they should be worried about me.

"I've come into the team and tried to be respectful of space and definitely not put the team in jeopardy. I stand by that and that's all I can talk about."

Team principal Frederic Vasseur said the incident between his two drivers was "not good". But he also was keen to stress that every team on the grid has to manage intra-team tensions.

"Now, to see if we have a team order or whatever, I think that the comparison that I made was that last year, [Oscar] Piastri was leading McLaren at this stage of the season, and if McLaren put everything on Piastri, [Red Bull's] Max Verstappen would have been champion.

"For sure, at one stage you have to make a decision, but I think it was too early to make a decision before Monza. Now we have time to discuss with the guys."

Hamilton said Ferrari needed to look at how they communicate.

"If we continue to travel the same path, we get the same result," he said. "And it's like we keep getting the same result. We've got to change things because it's not helping us to move forward. I think they're receptive to it and we'll take it offline."

Antonelli 'walks over water' for win that will go down in F1 folklore

Leclerc says throttle felt 'weird' before crash

Shortly after his fight with Hamilton, Leclerc's day then went from bad to worse as his shunt into the barriers ended any hopes of repeating his Monza successes of 2019 and 2024.

He was left sitting on the grass heartbroken after safely climbing out of the wrecked car, and Ferrari later confirmed the 28-year-old was OK after being checked over by medical staff.

"For the crash itself, I went on throttle [and] on the first lap it felt kind of weird; I had to go back off and on throttle," said Leclerc.

"On that second lap, I tried to do the same thing, but I don't know, it just felt a little bit weird. We'll look into it."

Leclerc said he would have additional medical checks but expected to be fine to compete at next weekend's Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid.

articles.title: To evade bike in  flooded lane, teen grabs pole, dies of shock in west Delhi
articles.summary: Delhi’s Bindapur: 13-year-old Kaushal dies after being found unconscious in a waterlogged lane; family alleges electrocution from an iron pipe near a pole.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A 13-year-old boy was found unconscious in a waterlogged lane in west Delhi’s Bindapur and later died Friday. His family has alleged that he died because he was electrocuted when he touched an iron pipe near an electricity pole.Kaushal was a Class 8 student of Sarvodaya Vidyalaya in Janakpuri and lived in Nand Ram Park, Bindapur. Police said information about the boy’s death came from BM Gupta Hospital to the Bindapur police station on Sept 4.The cops said Kaushal’s grandmother, Sridevi, found him unconscious about 50 metres from their home. She alerted his mother, Hemlata, who rushed him to the hospital, where doctors declared him brought dead. His body was shifted to DDU Hospital, where a postmortem was conducted Saturday.The family said the boy was walking through the waterlogged lane after heavy rain when a motorcycle passed by, rather close to him. Fearing he would fall, he allegedly grabbed an iron pipe attached to the electricity pole. The family and residents said the pipe emitted an electric shock that killed him. Locals reportedly pulled the boy away using a wooden stick, but he could not be saved.A senior police officer said the exact reason for his death will be established in the postmortem. Police are examining the circumstances surrounding it.Kaushal has a six-year-old sister. His father works at an optical shop in Rama Garden, while his mother is a homemaker.The family alleged that persistent waterlogging and electrical safety issues in the locality contributed to the boy’s death.Residents also claimed that the lane frequently remained waterlogged even after light rainfall and that sewage water accumulated there even when it was not raining. articles.title: Lewis Hamilton claims there are 'no rules' at Ferrari after clash with team-mate Charles Leclerc during Italian GP
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc made contact on the first lap of the Italian Grand Prix before the Brit ran onto the gravel and lost several positions; Hamilton fell 76 points behind championship leader Kimi Antonelli after the Mercedes driver came from 19th on the grid to win at Monza
articles.body:
Hamilton launched an aggressive move up the inside of his team-mate at the first corner, but was then forced off onto the gravel himself on the exit of the chicane as Leclerc held onto the inside line.

Hamilton dropped from his starting position of fourth to 10th, and was left playing catch-up for the rest of the race, as he eventually finished sixth.

Leclerc held onto third after the incident, which featured contact between the pair, but then crashed out of the race on the second lap, leaving Ferrari to suffer a dismal afternoon at their home race.

"I think it comes down to rules of engagement," said Hamilton, who joined Ferrari from Mercedes in 2025.

"When I was at Mercedes, we had written rules of engagement.

"We never really, really had it too bad. There was a moment between me and Nico [Rosberg] a couple of times, but more often not, it was good.

"Here, there are no rules. We need to address that."

Championship leader Kimi Antonelli claimed a stunning victory from 19th at the grid to extend his advantage over Hamilton to 76 points, while the Ferrari driver also fell 10 points behind George Russell as the Brit completed a Mercedes one-two.

It had been a topic of discussion in the media before the race as to whether Ferrari should prioritise Hamilton over Leclerc given his advantage in the standings, which was extended to 36 points by Sunday's result.

Asked by Sky Sports F1 after the race whether he should have priority over Leclerc, Hamilton replied: "We are too far past that already. It's too late for that now.

"I lost a lot of points today to those guys.

"We will do our best to keep pushing the rest of the season but they are out now, out ahead of us."

Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur insisted that it was too early in the season for the team to prioritise one of their drivers.

Vasseur justified his position by using the example of McLaren's experience last year, when Oscar Piastri led Lando Norris in the standings before being hauled in by both his team-mate and Max Verstappen by the end of the season.

"For sure, the outcome of the first corners is not good for the team," Vasseur said.

"Now, to see if we have a team order or whatever, I think that the good comparison that I made was that last year, Piastri was leading McLaren at this stage of the season and if McLaren put everything on Piastri, Max Verstappen would have been champion.

"For sure, at one stage you have to take a decision but I think it was too early to take a decision before Monza. Now we have time to discuss with the guys."

Leclerc admitted that he and Hamilton had gone "too far" in their early battle, but questioned who was "forcing" a narrative playing the team-mates off against each other.

The Monegasque referred to the previous race in Zandvoort when Hamilton had been left frustrated by being held up by Leclerc during the race when the pair were on different strategies.

"I don't really know who is forcing that narrative that we are one against the other," Leclerc said.

"I mean, honestly, Zandvoort, there was way too many talks already.

"Here, it's true though that we went too far. I think Lewis in Turn 1, then Turn 2, I tried to do the tightest corner possible, but that was just not enough - and doing it here is not good."

Hamilton was also once more left frustrated by his team's strategic decisions, with the 41-year-old questioning both the choice of tyre compound for him after the early red flag, and a later decision not to pit him under a virtual safety car.

"It's one of the harder ones to swallow today," he told Sky Sports F1. "I was definitely hoping for more.

"I gave it absolutely everything. We just didn't have the speed on the straights and we were mostly a sitting duck to the guys around me.

"We will look internally and try and figure out what we could have done better. I felt we should have been on the hard tyre [on the restart] but we also would have had to overtake people, because we were further back than we were supposed to be.

"I thought they were going to stop us [under the VSC] but they didn't stop us, so I ran out of tyres."

Vasseur said that Ferrari's difficultly overtaking due to a lack of straight-line speed meant they would have struggled to make an extra stop work in the way that Antonelli and Verstappen, who finished third, were able to.

"We were 10 seconds behind Max before the VSC and we finished 10 seconds behind," Vasseur told Sky Sports F1.

"If you do this [pit], you have to overtake and overtaking is not our favourite topic. It would have been more difficult."

articles.title: Italian Grand Prix: Kimi Antonelli's stunning Monza victory will go down in F1 folklore
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli delivered one of the great F1 drives to win the Italian Grand Prix and leave Mercedes' team-mate George Russell's title hopes almost a lost cause.
articles.body:
Kimi Antonelli's stunning victory in the Italian Grand Prix from 19th on the grid will go down in Formula 1 folklore - and, remarkably, his team boss Toto Wolff said that he had seen it coming on Saturday.

After Sunday's race, Wolff said that beforehand he thought that one of his two drivers was going to be standing on the top of the podium.

It was an eye-opening statement given they started the race 17 places apart on the grid, George Russell on the front row alongside shock pole winner Pierre Gasly's Alpine; Antonelli on the penultimate row.

"I thought one of the two is going to win," Wolff said. "Either George, because he was on the front row, or Kimi because he's going to walk over water, here at Monza. And I felt that yesterday also."

Wolff was asked to explain why he felt a performance he was comparing to a miracle was on the cards.

"It's been a while that I've seen drivers," he said. "Energy levels, mindset or behavioural pattern. I knew that was his mission today, to win the race. I chatted with his father yesterday. The father also saw that coming.

"These are the moments where you can see how a weekend is panning out through the sessions that a special moment can come."

Antonelli takes stunning Monza win from 19th on grid

Antonelli extraordinary as Gasly has superb weekend - driver ratings

For the Mercedes drivers, this race was all about the context of the weekend.

Antonelli knew coming in that he would be starting at the back because of a grid penalty for using too many engines this year.

Russell knew that he had to make the most of this opportunity and cut as much as he could out of his team-mate's 59-point championship lead.

Fifth or sixth was the general consensus for what might be realistically possible for Antonelli, who himself said after the race that he had "thought a podium was possible".

What changed everything was his remarkable progress in the early laps of the race, which brought to mind another Biblical miracle, the parting of the Red Sea.

Antonelli was 14th after a relatively conservative first lap, then 12th at the end of lap two, when Charles Leclerc crashed his Ferrari to bring the race to a temporary halt.

"With the red flag, I was already P12," Antonelli said. "And then I knew that I could have a shot at it."

A lap after the restart, he was up to eighth, and on the back of the leading group of cars running nose to tail. Seventh a lap later, after dispatching Lando Norris' McLaren.

By now, Russell was in the lead, having wasted little time dispensing with Gasly. But the Briton sensed trouble.

"A great race from the neutral perspective," Russell said. "As soon as I saw Kimi up to P5 after a handful of laps, I knew he was going to be in the fight with us. That was clearly a very impressive opening few laps."

Wolff said: "The differentiator today was the ability to go through the traffic. We've seen it with other great ones in the past. Lewis (Hamilton), who did it in some of the races. That's what he's shown today. When a driver and a car are one, then there's nothing that can stop them."

Antonelli in no mood to obey a computer algorithm

Briefly, for a few laps, Russell and Max Verstappen threatened to break away in the lead while Antonelli was finding a way past Gasly, the two McLarens and Hamilton's Ferrari.

But Russell and Verstappen were fighting at the front, costing each other time, and Antonelli was up to third by lap 13, just 1.8secs off Verstappen in the lead, with Russell between them.

Three laps later, the Mercedes drivers were running one-two, and starting to swap places themselves, until, with Russell leading, it was suggested by that team that they give it a rest and try to break away from Verstappen.

If Russell could not do so, they said, they would "invert the cars" - put Antonelli into the lead to try himself. But slowly they began to inch clear.

At this point, coming up to half-distance, the race victory was still up in the air. There was a virtual safety car (VSC), called when Lance Stroll's Aston Martin broke down at the first corner.

Mercedes called Antonelli for new tyres - a decision they had to make as he had switched to the medium compound at the red flag and that would not make it to the end. Russell continued on his hard tyres.

"It was the right thing to split the strategies," Wolff said, "because we didn't know what the better one would be. In the morning meeting, we said the hard tyre is going to go forever. You can start on it and finish on it. And you can see with George, it was a forever tyre.

"At that stage, the system said that the one-stop comes out ahead, that two-stop was coming close to the end, but didn't catch it. That's what the software said."

Antonelli was in no mood to obey a computer algorithm. Rejoining 14.3secs behind Russell, with 24 laps to go and four cars between them, winning was not an easy task. But he made it look like it.

Antonelli caught Russell with five laps to go and the win now looked inevitable. There was a hiccup when he ran off the track at turn one with four laps to go after Russell blocked his attack on the inside, and Antonelli lost grip on the loose rubber off line and slid into the gravel trap.

That dropped him to 1.7secs off again, but a lap and a half later, he drove past Russell on the straight between the second Lesmo corner and Ascari, and that was that.

The home fans, with split loyalties before the race between Antonelli and Ferrari, screamed with delight as he crossed the line, 60 years since the last time an Italian won his home race.

"It's one that I will remember forever," Antonelli said. "Definitely the fans gave that little bit extra to push more. The support has been great this weekend.

"Definitely seeing the grandstand cheering every lap it gave that little bit of extra to push more and to try and do even better to win it."

Far too late for title fight priority - Hamilton

'Circle closes' after 'everyone doubted' Antonelli in 2024

The win, Wolff said, was "how the circle closed" after Antonelli's difficult introduction to F1, when he crashed in a one-off outing in free practice at this race two years ago, a moment Wolff said was "probably the toughest moment in his career. For himself and his family. A moment where everyone doubted, including himself.

"Two years later, it's the biggest glory, the biggest moment of his career (so far). That's probably going to be one of his biggest (ever)."

A maiden season in F1 last year followed in which Antonelli showed flashes of promise but little that indicated what has happened this year would follow.

"When you talk about the complete driver, there's the aspect of experience that needs to come," Wolff said.

"There is also that he has this easiness of a young man that helps to overcome difficult moments. That also helps in managing not getting ahead of himself when having these glorious moments.

"There is the fact of is he capable of maturing, of staying the personality that he is, humble, with a lot of introspection, self-criticism, in order to develop. And that only the future is going to show - whether he is like a few drivers before him a complete deal.

"But it is still surprising and amazing to see how quickly he develops. For me, it's like an AI agent that continuously self-improves and learns. That's the speed. And there also, his age is for sure beneficial. The ability, cognitively, intellectually, to constantly become better."

Russell hurts with title almost a lost cause

After the race, Russell tried to put a brave face on it, but it was impossible not to see how much it was hurting him.

Speaking in the news conference, sentences ran out of steam, his voice was on the point of breaking at times.

Russell gently pointed out, in not quite so many words, that without the VSC he probably would have won - "it would have been very interesting to see how the race would have panned out if there was no VSC".

But he was well aware of what Antonelli's stellar performance meant. The strategy, he said, "takes nothing away from Kimi's drive altogether".

And the championship, he now knows, is almost a lost cause. Antonelli's win moves him 66 points clear.

Russell talked about "taking the positives", about how, after a "very tough run" in the early summer, since the season re-started in the Netherlands two weeks ago, "every lap, every session, I've been sort of in the mix of the top three positions, similar to where I was at the start of the year".

That's true. But there has not been a hint all year of Russell being able to put together a run of results where he consistently beats Antonelli, which is now his only hope.

"It's definitely Kimi's in control of it," Russell said. "And, you know, he's deserving to be in control of it.

"For me personally, I'm not even thinking about a fight or a comeback or anything. I'm just focused on taking it race by race and trying to maximise every single weekend.

"He's performing incredibly well. It's going to be exceptionally challenging to overcome that gap. So I'm just sort of accepting that is what it is."

articles.title: Kimi Antonelli: Mercedes driver hailed by pundits and Toto Wolff after remarkable 19th to first Italian GP comeback win
articles.summary: Nico Rosberg and Martin Brundle have their say on Kimi Antonelli's remarkable comeback drive as Mercedes' boss Toto Wolff explains what he felt made the difference; watch every session of the Spanish Grand Prix at a new track in Madrid from Friday, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
Of course, unlike surprise pole position sitter Pierre Gasly - who had never previously qualified at the head of an F1 grid in 190 appearances spent in mostly midfield cars - the 20-year-old Antonelli has become a fixture at the head of the field this year.

Sunday represented the seventh race win of the Mercedes driver's increasingly-impressive second of Formula 1 and one which extended what stood as a 59-point championship lead to a joint season-high 66 points.

But by winning from the second-lowest grid position in F1's 76-year history - 19th place - and beating a team-mate and chief title rival in George Russell who had started from the front row, Antonelli ensured it was anything but just another win.

And that's before you even consider the local factor too - Antonelli ended a 60-year wait for an Italian to win their home Grand Prix again.

The remarkable Monza comeback led to Antonelli being described as "King Kimi" by Martin Brundle, who has both raced against and commentated on many of the sport's most legendary figures over more than four decades.

Brundle's fellow Sky Sports F1 pundit Nico Rosberg, the 2016 world champion, was similarly effusive in his praise after witnessing Antonelli's remarkable drive.

"We have to say the race that he drove, the first lap, the second start, everything was to perfection," said Rosberg.

"The speed he had, how he was managing everything. You cannot do it better.

"He's in his second season in F1, he just turned 20. Who does that like that? It's just unheard of!"

'He's going to walk over water' - Wolff thought 'special moment' was possible

Rosberg had been among the many ahead of the race to suggest that a podium was likely out of Antonelli's reach from the grid's penultimate row, something the Italian himself had ruled out after qualifying.

But it turns out that not everyone was expecting it to necessarily be a race purely of damage limitation from the grid penalties that had left Antonelli so out of position.

"I thought one of the two [Mercedes drivers] is going to win," disclosed Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff after the race.

"Either George because he was on pole [for the restart] or Kimi because he's going to walk over water here in Monza. And I felt that yesterday also."

Wolff, who worked with Lewis Hamilton at Mercedes for six of the Briton's seven world titles, said he sensed "a special moment" was potentially in the offing from Antonelli at his home track.

"Its been a while that I've seen drivers' energy levels, mindset or behavioural pattern and I knew that that was his mission today, to win the race," he said.

"I chatted with his father yesterday, the father also saw that coming.

"These are the moments where you can see how a weekend is panning out through the sessions, that a special moment could come.

"It's still a mechanical sport, so it can change quickly."

Like any great comeback story, Antonelli's was not without some good fortune along the way.

Certainly, the second race start after the red flag for Charles Leclerc's big lap-two crash offered a second chance to make up multiple places more quickly than otherwise might have made the chance had the race not been stopped, even if it did compromise Mercedes' plans for running Antonelli on a long hard-tyre opening stint.

He was already running 12th by the time the red flag was thrown. He then picked up four more places on the restart lap. By lap 13 he was directly behind Russell in third and, once Gasly's early challenge faded, the Mercedes' went head-to-head from lap 16 in what soon turned into an almost lap-by-lap changing of the lead.

Eventually running second as the battle settled down slightly, a later well-timed Virtual Safety Car then allowed Antonelli to make a pit stop to switch on to fresher medium tyres, with Russell soon locked in to going to the end on more-worn hards, although Wolff said it was not clear at the time which strategy would win the race.

In any case, Wolff believes it was Antonelli's driving on track overtaking cars that made the difference.

"The differentiator today was the ability going through the traffic," added Wolff. "We've seen it with other great ones in the past. Lewis put it in some of the races and that's what he's shown today.

"There's just no stopping when a driver and a car are one, then there's nothing that can stop them."

As for Italy's rising star himself, Antonelli said he had woke up on Sunday morning feeling "very good mentally" and "that a very good result would have been a podium for me".

"But after the red flag I was already P12 and I had another start," he added.

"After another couple of laps I was already in the top five and I knew I could have a shot for the win. Of course it was very difficult to break away but we managed to pull it off and bring it home."

articles.title: La última carrera era lo de menos: Palou levanta su quinta Astor Cup
articles.standfirst: Una mala estrategia de neumáticos le impidió luchar por la victoria, pero la quinta copa ya es suya
articles.summary: Una mala estrategia de neumáticos le impidió luchar por la victoria, pero la quinta copa ya es suya
articles.body: Laguna Seca nunca había visto a Álex Palou bajarse del podio... hasta hoy. El español y su equipo, probablemente sin la motivación ni la tensión de jugarse algo, no encontraron el camino en una carrera que se les complicó desde el inicio. Aunque Palou partía en primera fila, lo hacía en inferioridad en cuanto a neumáticos. Porque sus dos primeros relevos fueron con blandas usadas y, aunque en el primer stint pudo mantenerse cerca de McLaughlin (con blandas nuevas) en el segundo se desangró (apenas le duró 14 vueltas) y ya no pudo enderezar el camino. Tuvo que parar antes de hora y, para colmo, salió en tráfico y se encontró bloqueado poco después con su primer juego de duras... usadas. Así que a mitad de carrera tuvo que hacer la tercera parada, casi a la vez que los líderes entraban por segunda vez... no había nada que hacer más que terminar de la forma más honrosa posible que, al menos, fue en el top 10 (octavo). El español había guardado los dos juegos nuevos que tenía (duros primero y blandos después) para la segunda parte de carrera... pero fue demasiado tarde. Pese a que se escapó el récord de poles ayer y la séptima victoria hoy, la temporada de Palou solo se puede calificar de sobresaliente. No llega al cum laude del año pasado... pero con un par de aspectos . Y el broche de oro llegó al final de la carrera, con la coronación y la entrega de la quinta Copa Astor... que no será la última que levante el piloto de San Antonio de Vilamajor (Barcelona). Con Palou fuera de combate, nadie pudo hacerle sombra al poleman, Scott McLaughlin (Penske), que termina el año con buen sabor de boca y con el consuelo de no irse de vacío (es su primera victoria de la temporada). Con Palou coronado y con un universo de ventaja sobre el resto, lo más interesante en juego en la final era el subcampeonato. Tres candidatos (Lundgaard, Kirkwood y O'Ward) separados sólo por cuatro puntos. Por lo tanto... el que acabara delante del resto se llevaba el premio de consolación. Y fue para Kyle Kirkwood (Andretti), el más entonado hoy desde el inicio y, en el fondo, el que más lo mereció durante toda la temporada. El estadounidense escaló posiciones rápidamente desde el sexto de parrilla y a mitad de carrera ya era segundo, posición que no abandonó ya hasta el final... aunque nunca pudo en peligro el triunfo de McLaughlin. Malukas estuvo al acecho toda la carrera, pero siempre con peor ritmo que Kirkwood y en desventaja de neumáticos con Rossi (Carpenter), que acabó en el podio aprovechando las blandas nuevas que puso en el último stint. Scott Dixon, seis veces ganador de la IndyCar, disputaba su última carrera con Ganassi después de más de 20 años en sus filas... y con un récord que no quería romper: 21 temporadas seguidas ganando al menos una carrera. Lo intentó con una estrategia alternativa, con paradas anticipadas que le permitieran escalar posiciones (salía 16º) si una amarilla le ayudaba... pero en un año en el que no le ha salido nada, la suerte tampoco estuvo con él esta vez. El año que viene intentará cambiarla en McLaren. Por la parte trasera de la tabla también había algo en juego: el rookie del año. La ventaja era enorme para el noruego Dennis Hauger (18 puntos de ventaja sobre Mick Schumacher)... pero se le complicó nada más empezar al recibir un impacto por detrás de Sting Ray Robb en la primera vuelta que le hizo perder todas sus opciones. Claro que para que el alemán pudiera hacerse con el galardón necesitaba hacer un gran resultado... y aún no está para eso en IndyCar (quizá el año que viene, en el equipo MSR, sea diferente...). La temporada 2026 de la IndyCar ha terminado... y ahora la competición americana de monoplazas tendrá la habitual postemporada 'eterna'... ya que el arranque del año 2027 no llegará hasta el 7 de marzo, en St. Pete (Florida).

articles.title: NASCAR Playoffs Bracket 2026 Point Standings After Darlington Round of 16 Results
articles.summary: Christopher Bell used a late pass of Kyle Larson to claim the Southern 500 and his first win of the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series season.
articles.body:
Christopher Bell used a late pass of Kyle Larson to claim the Southern 500 and his first win of the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series season.

Bell benefited from the better pit strategy after a brief rain delay and passed Larson with 11 laps remaining in one of NASCAR's crown jewel races.

Live Sunday Night's Main Event Updates 📝

The victory allowed Bell to surge up the playoff point standings. He is now within 12 points of points leader Denny Hamlin.

Bell's win awarded him the most points on the night and a giant sense of relief after seven second-place finishes this season.

Bell placed in the top five on 11 occasions prior to Sunday night's victory.

The driver of the No. 20 car won the race with 11 laps to go with his pass of Kyle Larson.

Larson and a few others opted not to pit under the final caution. That risk didn't pay off, as Bell and his fresh tires took over the lead.

Bell's Joe Gibbs Racing teammate Ty Gibbs also benefited from the fresh tires to finish the race in second place.

Larson tumbled all the way back to fifth place. Tyler Reddick claimed third and Ryan Blaney took fourth.

Bell pushed himself all the way up to second place in the points standings with the win. He is 12 points back of Denny Hamlin. The top four drivers in the standings are within 24 points of each other.

The Chase for the Cup Series title continues next Sunday at Worldwide Technology Raceway.

The driver with the most points after the 10th playoff race will be named the 2026 Cup Series champion.

articles.title: ¡Que viene el Madring!: "Está entre Jeddah y Mónaco, no hay lugar al fallo"
articles.standfirst: Aston Martin sale de un fin de semana frustrante en Monza, pero encara con energías renovadas el Gran Premio de España
articles.summary: Aston Martin sale de un fin de semana frustrante en Monza, pero encara con energías renovadas el Gran Premio de España
articles.body: El resumen de Aston Martin en Monza se explica poco antes de cumplirse las 30 vueltas del Gran Premio de Italia. Fernando Alonso abandonaba en su patinete el tv-pen tras otro abandono; Lawrence Stroll, dueño de la estructura, entraba al hospitality y Lance Stroll aparecía desde la otra parte del circuito tras un problema hidráulico. Cero puntos, lo esperado. Dos abandonos, la peor noticia posible. Lo mejor es que en siete días todo puede cambiar. Viene el Madring. El Gran Premio de España es un panorama diferente, con menos dependencia del motor y un chasis del AMR26 que marca diferencias. "Desde el punto de vista de la simulación, deberíamos estar en un lugar mejor. Lo dijo Fernando [Alonso] anteriormente: hay circuitos que nos sientan mejor. Otros peor. Sabíamos que Monza no nos iba bien, pero el mejor lugar es posible aunque sea difícil de decir tras lo que ocurrió. Y tampoco conocemos el circuito, sólo tenemos los datos de simulación y será un desafío", analizó Mike Krack ante los medios desplazados a Italia, con MARCA presente. El ingeniero jefe en pista de los británicos, además, es positivo. "Os veo la sonrisa. Lo esperamos con ganas", bromeó frente ante la prensa española. El trazado de IFEMA-Valdebebas se presenta en sociedad tras un test de Fórmula 3 que asustó por las banderas rojas, los chasis para el desguace y la distancia con los muros. Y no es sencillo ni de clasificar. Krack lo intenta dibujar con dos ejemplos de vértigo, velocidad y riesgo: "Será una pista que evolucione mucho. Pero con lo que he visto, creo que será excitante, lo clasifico entre Jeddah y Mónaco". Con una justificación más sencilla si cabe. "El muro está muy cerca y no hay lugar para el fallo", argumentó. Es la línea de pensamiento que parece extenderse entre los jefes de equipo de la Fórmula 1. También James Vowles, máximo responsable de Williams, puso sobre la mesa los riesgos a tomar. "Es un circuito que no existe parecido en el calendario, ya es una propiedad única. En los F3 vimos nueve banderas rojas, tres chasis rotos, seis suspensiones... Sí, son pilotos de F3, pero es una pista asesina de coches y será interesante", señaló. Eso sí, ponía en duda la degradación que a Aston le vendría de perlas. "Si hay, lo abrazamos", expresó Krack. El factor limitante de Aston Martin seguirá siendo Honda. No se espera que Madrid dependa demasiado de la unidad de potencia, pero deben evitarse problemas como el fallo en los componentes eléctricos del sábado en Italia. Lo mejor: la manejabilidad. "Estoy feliz porque dimos un paso en ese contexto. El coche es más predecible y el piloto encuentra el límite más fácil. Y si el coche es consistente, pues puedes ir más cerca de los límites. De lo contrario habrá margen que tomar", confesó Krack. Su homónimo en el cargo en Honda también lo validaba. "Lo principal era comprobar si las medidas funcionaron y parece que hay comportamiento positivo. Tenemos sensaciones positivas y lo vemos en los datos, es clave para Madrid porque será vital", analizó. En el otro lado de la balanza, los problemas. Si bien hay un paso en la combustión que los pilotos no notan tanto, en otros aspectos hay defectos como el componente eléctrico. "Es algo que debemos arreglar, entendemos que algo falla en las cinco o seis partes que hemos cambiado", cerró Alonso.

articles.title: NASCAR pays $1,115 after drivers swore 223 times on the radio during Southern 500 race
articles.summary: NASCAR's new promotion is off to a great (bleeping) start, where fans have a chance to win money if they can accurately guess how many times drivers will swe...
articles.body:
NASCAR is pledging $5 to a swear jar throughout the final ten races of the year for every moment when a Cup Series driver swears on the radio ... and it didn't take long for the jar start filling up.

Drivers were caught swearing on the radio 223 times during the Southern 500 at Darlington, and we know for a fact Ryan Blaney was responsible for several of those moments. Fans were joking how the 2023 champion, known for his temper on the radio, would be one of the top swearers during this promotion and he did not disappoint.

With 223 different swear words caught on the radio, the jar hit $1,115 following the grueling opening round of the Chase.

Fans can visit HERE and try and guess how many swear words there will be throughout the Chase. To put it simply, anyone who guesses correctly will win the money in the jar. This is part of NASCAR's 'Hell Yeah' campaign for 2026, which promises to bring the sport back to its roots.

Even race winner Christopher Bell dropped a 'damn' in his post-race interview, but sadly, we don't think that one counts since he was out of the car at that point.

articles.body:
4.15 Windsor - Classy Raaheeb aims to resume his progression

The classy Raaheeb aims to resume his progression in the Weatherbys Global Stallions App Winter Hill Stakes .

A brother to top class performers Baaeed and Hukum, Raaheeb began his career perfectly with a nice success at two, before taking the Classic Trial at Sandown in terrific fashion. He then ran creditably when fourth in the Irish Derby, travelling up like a genuine challenger before tiring late under Rossa Ryan.

The time given to help Raaheeb develop physically and mentally could set him up for a nice return to the track and he should be tough to beat in calmer waters, even under a penalty.

Venetian Prince goes for the in-form Andrew Balding yard, having won the Italian Derby in June. However, Jason Watson's mount will have to put a Royal Ascot no-show behind him, when he was outpaced over three furlongs out in the King Edward VII Stakes.

Conversely, Maho Bay ran creditably at the Royal meeting and connections could have considered themselves unlucky to have ran into trouble in the home straight. He remains unexposed and can provide the biggest threat for a yard going well.

Crest Of Fire and Harmonics have been progressing through handicaps but would need to take a significant step forward to win up in grade.

4.00 Newton Abbot - Improving duo Arctic Voyage and Edelak feature in cagey affair

The improving duo of Arctic Voyage and Edelak feature in a cagey Par Inn Handicap Hurdle .

Edelak resumed winning ways at Stratford in July after falling on his penultimate start when a likely winner. He has now won four of his last five - and doing so rather easily - with a small break after a busy period likely to see him put in a career best.

However, the opposition is tough with Arctic Voyage taking very well to hurdling since switching to the Michael Blake yard. He has won three of his last four and looked particularly good last time out when scoring with a fair bit in hand.

Although on a fair mark and back over hurdles, War Correspondent has not had the best preparation coming into this with two poor runs over fences, so Ellerton is the main threat to the former two with an encouraging win back over hurdles on his CV after a breathing operation.

6.30 Wolverhampton - Progressive filly Brunhilde steps up in trip

Progressive filly Brunhilde steps up in trip in the Follow @attheraces On Instagram Handicap .

George Boughey's filly has progressed with each run since making her debut in May and connections' patience was rewarded when she won by over five lengths at Lingfield when last seen. She is stoutly bred, being closely related to Godolphin's listed winner Ghostwatch, so the step up to one-mile and six furlongs should yield more improvement.

Last Verse won very nicely at Lingfield on his last start and remains relatively unexposed and on the right side of the handicap.

Level Look should be able to progress from his promising Chester second place after being at a disadvantage when too far back at the Shergar Cup last month.

Robusto won last time and can be competitive, albeit his higher all-weather mark means he has less scope in his mark than his more unexposed rivals.

articles.title: Tragedia en el motor: muere el piloto Pablo Amorós tras un accidente en Monteblanco
articles.standfirst: Competía en la GTI Trophy en el trazado onubense cuando llegó el fatal desenlace
articles.summary: Competía en la GTI Trophy en el trazado onubense cuando llegó el fatal desenlace
articles.body: Tragedia en el mundo del motor de España. El piloto Pablo Amorós falleció el domingo 6 de septiembre cuando disputaba una cita del GTI Trophy, una competición monomarca en la que todos los pilotos comparten la pase del Volkswagen Golf IV GTI preparado para los circuitos. El terrible accidente ocurrido en el trazado de Monteblanco, en Huelva, ha causado una consternación máxima tras la pérdida de uno de los grandes veteranos de los circuitos en nuestro país. Amorós era un competidor amateur y abogado de profesión, pero contaba con sobrada experiencia tanto en los rallyes, con buenos resultados en competiciones todoterreno; así como en circuitos, pues se prodigaba en competiciones como la Copa Kobe o el propio GTI. Además, no era extraño verle rodar en el Jarama, uno de los lugares en los que siempre se le recordará con mayor fuerza. Como es lógico, las causas del accidente todavía están siendo investigadas. Lo que parece si se atiende a las pocas imágenes televisivas de la retransmisión, es que hubo algún tipo de problema mecánico en el Golf que desencadenó los hechos. En la curva 1 después de un relanzamiento llegaba a una velocidad muy superior, no pudo parar el coche e impactó con otro piloto. El competidor que recibió el golpe también fue atendido de inmediato en la pista onubense. "Desde la organización del GTI Trophy lamentamos profundamente comunicar el fallecimiento del piloto Pablo Amorós durante el transcurso de la carrera celebrada hoy en el Circuito de Monteblanco (Huelva). Queremos trasladar nuestras más sinceras condolencias y nuestro apoyo a su familia, amigos y seres queridos en estos momentos tan difíciles”, comunicó la organización del campeonato justo después de lo ocurrido en la pista de La Palma del Condado, circuito habitual de competiciones nacionales, apto para tandas y todo tipo de vehículos de carreras. Todas las instituciones importantes del motor español reaccionaron al instante trasladando las condolencias por el fallecimiento de uno de pilotos que invertía su dinero, tiempo y esfuerzos en su mayor pasión. Descanse en Paz.

articles.title: El desastre de Monza: Hamilton explota y Ferrari pide perdón
articles.standfirst: Sólo un sexto del británico es el balance de la Scuderia en la cita de su casa
articles.summary: Sólo un sexto del británico es el balance de la Scuderia en la cita de su casa
articles.body: "Hemos fallado", decían desde el box de la Scuderia Ferrari mientras el homenaje a su mito Michael Schumacher se apagaba y los elogios iban para el italiano que los de Maranello, o Arrivabene más bien, no quisieron. La victoria de Kimi Antonelli en Monza se anteponía al bajón de la escudería más laureada con Fred Vasseur, su jefe, pidiendo perdón prácticamente. Su Gran Premio de Italia se acabó en un par de vueltas. El viernes salieron con su típica fuerza en casa y ya se veía que no era el coche más fuerte pese al nuevo ADUO. Pero el sábado ya se entendió que habría dificultades tras salvar la Q2 por una milésima. Lo que no esperaban era el golpe del domingo. Con una pelea entre Lewis Hamilton y Charles Leclerc en la Primera Variante, el brutal choque del monegasco en la Parabólica tras ir encendido y un sexto del heptacampeón como único botín. Es el peor Monza de Ferrari desde el doble abandono de Leclerc y Sebastian Vettel en 2020 y puede romper todo el trabajo de una temporada en la que ven el Mundial más lejos. Hamilton ya está a 76 de Antonelli y volvió a arremeter ante su equipo. La cerrada de Charles en la 1 le dejó sin opciones, aunque no parece un movimiento más allá de uno de carrera. Eso sí, entre compañeros de equipo... "Yo no compito sucio. Soy limpio, justo y dejo espacio. No quiero poner al equipo en peligro", adelantó. Y señaló a Leclerc: "Son reglas de compromiso. Cuando estaba en Mercedes las había y no iba mal. Sólo tuve un par de momentos con Nico [Rosberg] y ya. Y mucho mejor con Valtteri [Bottas]. Aquí no hay reglas y lo necesitamos arreglar". Un golpe duro sobre su compañero, con la comparación de su etapa gloriosa... aunque no menciona que allí sí fue a más con el choque con Rosberg en Barcelona como joya de la corona. El movimiento de Leclerc seguirá muy presente. Y el equipo tiene claro que algo debe cambiar. Con las famosas órdenes de equipo planeando por encima de todos. "Lo de las curvas 1-2 no fue positivo. Pero es pronto para decir si habrá órdenes. El año pasado Piastri iba lanzado y con órdenes, pues sería campeón Verstappen. Habrá que tomar una decisión en algún momento, pero es pronto. Hay tiempo para discutirlo", comentó Vasseur. Su preocupación es un Madring que conocen y donde tienen ventaja clara, y también terminar de asegurarse que Leclerc está al 100%. El accidente superó los 50G y la visión en un ojo se resintió tras el fortísimo impacto. "El cuello está bien, fue la visión al principio. No veía bien por el ojo derecho, pero luego fue bien. Hay dolores en algunas zonas, pero es normal", cerró el monegasco. Su intención es participar sin problemas en el inminente Gran Premio de España.

articles.title: TAG Heuer crea un nuevo Carrera, muy español, para 'su' GP de F1 en Madring
articles.standfirst: La firma suiza, sponsor titular del GP de España, reloj oficial de la F1 y de Red Bull Racing, lanza una preciosa versión de uno de sus iconos, con motivo de la primera cita en Madrid
articles.summary: La firma suiza, sponsor titular del GP de España, reloj oficial de la F1 y de Red Bull Racing, lanza una preciosa versión de uno de sus iconos, con motivo de la primera cita en Madrid
articles.body: Desde su fundación, hace más de 160 años, TAG Heuer ha entendido la relojería como una cuestión de precisión, pero también de velocidad, innovación y desafío. Su historia es, en buena medida, la historia de cómo la técnica aprendió a medir el tiempo cuando el tiempo dejó de ser estático. Desde los primeros cronómetros de salpicadero hasta los instrumentos de alta frecuencia concebidos para el deporte de competición, la manufactura suiza ha desarrollado mecanismos capaces de convertir cada fracción de segundo en información útil. Una filosofía que encuentra en el automovilismo su escenario natural: cuando todo sucede más deprisa, medir el tiempo ya no basta; hay que dominarlo. Ahora, con la llegada de la Fórmula 1 a Madrid y mientras la capital española se prepara para escribir un nuevo capítulo en la historia del automovilismo, TAG Heuer vuelve a poner el cronógrafo deportivo en el centro de la escena a través de uno de los pilares de su colección Carrera: el TAG Heuer Carrera Chronograph Sport. TAG Heuer Carrera Chronograph Sport Spain Limited Edition: un reloj para una carrera histórica La llegada de la Fórmula 1 a Madrid merecía algo más que una celebración, reclamaba un objeto capaz de conservarla en el tiempo. Con motivo de la primera edición del Formula 1 TAG Heuer Gran Premio de España 2026, la firma suiza presenta el TAG Heuer Carrera Chronograph Sport Spain Limited Edition, una interpretación exclusiva del nuevo cronógrafo de 42 mm creada específicamente para esta ocasión. La base técnica es la del nuevo Carrera Chronograph Sport, pero su lenguaje visual incorpora referencias inequívocas al país anfitrión. Los detalles en rojo y amarillo de las agujas centrales del cronógrafo y de la correa de piel perforada evocan los colores de España y aportan al conjunto una dosis adicional de energía. El gesto más especial, sin embargo, se encuentra en la parte posterior. El fondo de zafiro incorpora el grabado 'Spain Limited Edition', convirtiendo cada pieza en algo más que un reloj: en un testimonio de la primera carrera de Fórmula 1 celebrada en un circuito urbano en Madrid. TAG Heuer no se limita a diseñar un reloj para recordar el acontecimiento; construye alrededor de él una experiencia de coleccionista. Cada unidad se presenta acompañada de una lámina numerada y firmada por el reconocido artista contemporáneo español Manu Campa, cuya mirada sobre el automóvil y la cultura del motor conecta de manera natural con el ADN de la marca. El artista también es el responsable del exclusivo estuche concebido para esta edición. El resultado es un objeto en el que convergen tres códigos: la ingeniería relojera suiza, la cultura de la competición y la identidad creativa española. TAG Heuer Carrera Chronograph Sport: el cronógrafo vuelve a acelerar Los nuevos TAG Heuer Carrera Chronograph Sport no son una simple actualización estética, son una reinterpretación integral de un cronógrafo concebido desde su origen para vivir en movimiento. La ambición es tan clara como exigente: llevar el cronógrafo deportivo de nuevo a primera línea mediante una combinación más afinada de diseño, ergonomía y carácter competitivo. La transformación empieza, literalmente, por la caja. Uno de los cambios más relevantes reside en sus nuevas proporciones. El diámetro se reduce de 44 a 42 mm, mientras que la distancia entre asas pasa de 49,8 a 48,6 mm. No se trata de una reducción meramente numérica: estas nuevas dimensiones modifican de forma sustancial la presencia del reloj sobre la muñeca. El resultado es una arquitectura más equilibrada, más versátil y, sobre todo, más ergonómica. También se ha trabajado el perfil. El grosor desciende de 15,48 a 14,17 mm, una reducción que permite que el reloj se adapte con mayor naturalidad a la muñeca y adquiera una silueta considerablemente más depurada. El Carrera Chronograph Sport conserva así la contundencia visual que se espera de un cronógrafo deportivo, pero elimina buena parte del volumen innecesario. Es una evolución que no busca llamar la atención a cualquier precio, busca algo más difícil: conseguir que cada milímetro tenga una razón de ser.

articles.title: Las lágrimas de Colapinto tras un fallo dramático
articles.standfirst: El argentino peleaba por primera vez en las posiciones de cabeza, pero cometió un error del que se lamentó ante las televisiones
articles.summary: El argentino peleaba por primera vez en las posiciones de cabeza, pero cometió un error del que se lamentó ante las televisiones
articles.body: El equipo Alpine fue un claro protagonista del Gran Premio de Italia. Logró con Pierre Gasly la primera pole de su historia bajo el nombre de la firma de deportivos franceses y la primera para Enstone desde Fernando Alonso en Hungría 2009 con el Renault R29. En carrera, el francés cayó al séptimo y Franco Colapinto sumó un noveno que pudo ser mucho más. Y le provocó una situación triste que desembocó en sus lágrimas al bajarse del coche. Colapinto se rompió frente a las televisiones con derechos (Fox, ESPN, DAZN y TUDN) en castellano. "Fue una carrera dura, muy frustrante y triste porque no aproveché la gran oportunidad", comentó. Justo después, no podía evitar las lágrimas. "Podría haber sido una gran carrera, pero hubo un gran error. Desaproveché una oportunidad para el equipo y para mí", añadió. El piloto de Pilar se encontraba en las posiciones de cabeza tras una buena salida y la oportunidad que se generó tras el choque de Leclerc en la Parabólica. Batallaba con Verstappen, Piastri o Hamilton, pero en Lesmo todo cambió. Se fue ancho, pisó grava y cayó muy lejos en la clasificación. De su mejor puesto virtual en un tú a tú en la Fórmula 1 a un drama. "Es un poco triste. Pero toca aprender de esto y seguir", cerró. Lo mejor fue su capacidad de volver a pelear, ascender posiciones con un coche que volaba en Italia y cerrar la carrera en noveno. Sólo Gasly, con su mismo coche y partiendo en pole, y Arvid Lindblad mejoraron las prestaciones del argentino en los coches de la zona media. Para sus intereses, la mejor noticia es que el Alpine está. Recibió las mejoras que Gasly había estrenado en Holanda y su coche en Italia funcionó entre su reducción de peso y las piezas específicas para la alta velocidad. Además, aterrizará en Madrid, una ciudad donde residió en el pasado y en la que le abrazan como uno más. No en vano, tanto la Fórmula 1 como el Gran Premio de España le colocan en los carteles promocionales junto a los dos locales, Carlos Sainz y Fernando Alonso.

articles.standfirst: La disputa de la carrera de Madring supondrá importantes cambios en la movilidad en toda la zona de Valdebebas
articles.summary: La disputa de la carrera de Madring supondrá importantes cambios en la movilidad en toda la zona de Valdebebas
articles.body: Es el momento: el Gran Premio de España de Fórmula 1 llega a Madrid y el Ayuntamiento ya ha definido el dispositivo especial de movilidad que regulará el tráfico alrededor del circuito de Madring entre el 10 y el 14 de septiembre. Los espectadores sin acreditación no podrán acercarse al circuito en su vehículo particular y los residentes de las zonas más próximas necesitarán un permiso para acceder. Se espera que el Gran Premio de España de Fórmula 1 reúna a alrededor de 345.000 espectadores entre el viernes 11 y el domingo 13 de septiembre en el entorno de IFEMA y Valdebebas. Una concentración de público que obligará a transformar durante varios días la movilidad de esta zona de la capital. La principal recomendación para cualquier aficionado es muy clara: acudir en transporte público. El Ayuntamiento establecerá un perímetro de tráfico restringido alrededor del circuito al que no podrán acceder los vehículos particulares del público general, salvo que dispongan de la correspondiente acreditación. El dispositivo no afectará únicamente a quienes tengan una entrada para el Gran Premio. Los vecinos de barrios próximos, los trabajadores de las empresas de la zona, los hoteles, los servicios de reparto e incluso quienes pretendan atravesar el entorno de IFEMA también deberán tener en cuenta los cortes y controles. Las puertas del circuito de Madring estarán abiertas al público general entre las 8:00 y las 20:00 horas durante los tres días del Gran Premio, del viernes 11 al domingo 13 de septiembre. En el caso de determinadas entradas, actos privados o actividades corporativas, la salida podrá retrasarse hasta las 23:00 horas. El circuito dispondrá de 23 puertas distribuidas por todo su perímetro. Antes de iniciar el desplazamiento será importante comprobar cuál es el acceso correspondiente a cada entrada, ya que Madring está dividido en dos grandes sectores —norte y sur— y acudir al lado equivocado puede obligar a realizar un recorrido considerable. Todas las puertas dispondrán de un carril accesible para facilitar la entrada de las personas con movilidad reducida. El público general no podrá acceder libremente en coche al entorno inmediato del circuito. Entre el 11 y el 13 de septiembre se activará una corona interior de seguridad con tráfico restringido y accesos controlados. Dentro de ese perímetro no podrán entrar los espectadores en vehículos particulares sin acreditación, los coches que pretendan aparcar en las inmediaciones del circuito, los taxis y VTC fuera de los recorridos y zonas habilitadas, los vehículos de reparto sin permiso o fuera de su franja horaria, los trabajadores que no dispongan de acreditación y vehículos que únicamente quieran atravesar la zona. El plan contempla 11.854 plazas para coches, 1.000 para motocicletas y 270 para autocares, repartidas entre público general, clientes de hospitalidad y vehículos vinculados a la organización. Por tanto, disponer de una entrada para la carrera no significa que se pueda aparcar automáticamente junto al circuito: será necesario consultar previamente qué estacionamientos están asociados a cada tipo de acceso. Además, la M-11 y la M-40 podrán sufrir cortes puntuales si se produce una llegada masiva de vehículos o aparecen problemas de congestión. Las restricciones no se limitarán a los tres días de actividad en pista. Desde el jueves 10 hasta el lunes 14 de septiembre permanecerán cerradas al tráfico no autorizado varias calles situadas dentro del perímetro de Madring. Los cortes afectarán, total o parcialmente, a vías como: Avenida de las Fuerzas Armadas, Camino Viejo de Burgos, Vía de Dublín, Ribera del Sena, Ribera del Loira, Avenida del Consejo de Europa y Avenida de Alejandro de la Sota. También habrá controles y posibles desvíos en un perímetro exterior que incluye la Avenida de Logroño, la M-11, la M-12, la R-2, la M-40, la Avenida de Manuel Fraga Iribarne y otros accesos a Valdebebas e IFEMA. Por ello, incluso los conductores que no tengan como destino el Gran Premio deberían evitar la zona y buscar rutas alternativas durante esos días. El Metro será una de las principales formas de llegar al circuito. La línea 8, que conecta Nuevos Ministerios con Feria de Madrid y el aeropuerto, aumentará un 50 % su capacidad habitual y podrá transportar entre 15.000 y 21.000 viajeros por hora y sentido. También se reforzará la línea 4, con dos trenes adicionales en las horas punta y la línea 5, con un tren adicional en los momentos de mayor demanda. Metro incrementará igualmente la presencia de personal de información y seguridad en las estaciones más utilizadas. Cercanías reforzará sus servicios hacia Valdebebas. El viernes se prevé alcanzar una capacidad de 10.000 pasajeros por hora en los periodos de mayor afluencia, con intervalos de entre cinco y siete minutos. El sábado y el domingo circularán trenes cada cinco minutos en dos franjas clave: de 8:00 a 11:00 horas, coincidiendo con la llegada de los aficionados y de 15:30 a 19:30 horas, durante la salida del circuito. Fuera de esos periodos se mantendrán conexiones con Chamartín y el aeropuerto. Una de las grandes novedades será la puesta en marcha de cinco líneas gratuitas de autobús, que comunicarán Madring con algunos de los principales intercambiadores de Madrid y permitirán desplazarse entre las zonas norte y sur del recinto. Las líneas urbanas 171, 174, N28, 120, 122, 104, T11, 87, 172SF, 125 y 172 mantendrán su servicio, pero podrán sufrir desvíos y dejar de realizar algunas paradas situadas dentro del perímetro restringido. También se modificará la línea interurbana 828, que conecta Madrid y Canillejas con Alcobendas y la Universidad Autónoma. Durante los tres días del evento realizará 39 expediciones diarias, con frecuencias de entre 35 y 65 minutos. Los viajeros habituales de estas líneas deberán consultar los recorridos provisionales antes de desplazarse. Los taxis y los vehículos VTC tendrán puntos diferentes de recogida y bajada de viajeros, tanto en el sector norte como en el sur. En la zona norte los taxis utilizarán una parada situada en la Avenida de las Fuerzas Armadas. Los VTC recogerán y dejarán pasajeros en la Avenida de José Antonio Corrales. En la zona sur la bolsa de taxis se encontrará en los aparcamientos del Parque Juan Carlos I. También se permitirá dejar pasajeros en la Avenida de los Andes, entre las calles Petunias y Boj. Los VTC dispondrán de una zona próxima a la Calle Añil, junto a la M-40. Los VTC solo podrán entrar en estas zonas cuando tengan un servicio contratado previamente. No se permitirá que permanezcan allí esperando clientes. Los residentes del barrio de Las Cárcavas podrán acceder a sus viviendas, pero tendrán que hacerlo mediante una acreditación específica para sus vehículos. La organización será la encargada de distribuir estos permisos. La Policía Municipal establecerá controles en las entradas del barrio para impedir que los espectadores utilicen sus calles como aparcamiento alternativo. El objetivo es mantener las plazas disponibles para los residentes y evitar que el tráfico del Gran Premio se desplace hacia las zonas residenciales. También necesitarán acreditación los vehículos que quieran acceder a las oficinas y empresas situadas dentro del perímetro, los hoteles de la zona, el Club de Golf (solo podrán acceder los vehículos con una reserva para ese fin de semana y que estén correctamente acreditados) o el aparcamiento del Olivar. El dispositivo incluirá prohibiciones temporales de estacionamiento en varias calles próximas al circuito. Estas restricciones se señalizarán con al menos 48 horas de antelación. Los vehículos que continúen estacionados una vez que entre en vigor la prohibición podrán ser retirados por la grúa municipal. Por ello, los residentes y trabajadores de la zona deberán prestar especial atención a la señalización instalada durante los días anteriores al Gran Premio. En resumen, el plan permitirá mantener el acceso a viviendas, oficinas y establecimientos, pero la circulación diaria en los alrededores de IFEMA y Valdebebas quedará profundamente condicionada entre el 10 y el 14 de septiembre. Para los espectadores, la fórmula más sencilla será combinar Metro o Cercanías con alguna de las cinco lanzaderas gratuitas y evitar intentar llegar hasta las puertas del circuito en vehículo particular.

articles.title: Italian GP: Martin Brundle's verdict on Kimi Antonelli fairytale, 'bruised' George Russell and Lewis Hamilton-Charles Leclerc incident
articles.summary: Sky Sports F1's Martin Brundle on Kimi Antonelli's fairytale Monza victory at the Italian Grand Prix, Mercedes' decision to split their drivers' strategies and the opening lap incident between Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton
articles.body:
On a track where very low tyre degradation used to generate long periods of a train of cars simply following each other, this was relentless overtaking and counter-attack.

And of course, the fairytale victory of Italian hero Kimi Antonelli who went from 19th on the grid into the lead just 18 laps later.

His opening lap was a perfect combination of patience, guile and risk at the right moment. He was cautious into the first perilous chicane, and then behind Yuki Tsunoda's Racing Bull around the outside of the first Lesmo bend, and then again into the Ascari chicane, and then he squeezed down the right-hand side, close to the grass, of two cars down the next straight.

There have been two red flags at Monza F1 this century, in 2020 and 2026, both for Charles Leclerc crashing a Ferrari at the final Parabolica corner. Leclerc turned in a little wide after defending from Oscar Piastri's McLaren and then proceeded to accelerate hard towards the main pit straight.

Unfortunately, his left-rear tyre was on the green painted strip which includes a drain cover, and this put the Ferrari into a slide, and when he corrected the steering wheel by turning into that slide in the normal way, the front tyres suddenly found a lot of grip and twisted him hard into the barriers with a 60G crash. He was shaken and likely winded, but otherwise appeared to be largely in one piece, and hopefully fit for Madrid this coming weekend.

After the race I was told by a trusted source that the Ferrari has a propensity to spike a little in power in situations like that, even on the simulator, but that was not from the team.

The resultant red flag was a pain for George Russell who was leading nicely, having passed sensational pole-sitter Pierre Gasly's Alpine heading into lap two, and was setting about building a nice lead.

The red flag helped Kimi Antonelli nicely, he was already up to P12 and any field spread to the leaders was eliminated with a second standing start from the grid. Everyone was able to change tyres as per the regulations, which would mean a 50-lap run ahead on the same rubber for many drivers, including George Russell.

Leclerc was 'likely miffed' by Hamilton in first chicane incident

Leclerc had already had a skirmish on the first lap with team-mate Lewis Hamilton. Ferrari had promised and expected so much at this race, Hamilton even talking in terms of what it would mean to win in Monza for the team. But, in reality, they struggled throughout and just squeezed through Q2 qualifying into the top-10 shoot-out. Both drivers put a decent final lap together and with Piastri being penalised three grid spots for blocking Liam Lawson in Q2, and Antonelli confined to the back of the grid with power-unit penalties, the Ferraris lined up side by side on the second row.

Into the first chicane Hamilton released the brakes and rolled up the inside of Leclerc, forcing him wide and meaning a tight entry into the immediate Turn 2. They were side by side and Hamilton stuck it out around the outside. A likely miffed Leclerc understeered wide on that inside line and nerfed Hamilton off into the gravel. He could have given him more room most likely but clearly didn't want to.

There are necessarily comprehensive rules of engagement in general combat, and chicanes are often treated as one corner in that respect, but the whole scenario is seen through a different lens with the inevitable close contact on the opening lap. After all, we enjoy starting them as a tight pack.

The stewards reviewed it and decided no further action meaning it was a racing incident. Whatever the rules, if you're on the outside of Turn 2 in Monza at any point, you're highly likely to be run out of road and end up high on the exit kerb or in the gravel. We've all been there.

Russell will feel bruised by race-changing VSC

Antonelli cleared the rest of the pack in highly-impressive style and, I would imagine, much to Russell's surprise and chagrin, filling his mirrors. There then ensued a thrilling Mercedes cat-and-mouse game of overtaking and re-passing, always trying to maximise engine and battery energy for general lap time, attack and defence.

If within a second of the car in front they all get 'overtake mode' (at all circuits) which allows for charging the battery by an extra half a megajoule, and to keep a higher top speed for longer. All very handy with four long straights.

But as they fought this helped Max Verstappen stay in touch, as usual Max was driving the wheels off his Red Bull despite being fundamentally slower than the Mercs. He led at one stage and simply wouldn't give up. Finally, the Mercedes pit wall asked their drivers to stop racing each other and build a gap to Verstappen, and keep him well out of the overtake mode, and they duly obliged.

Then on Lap 28 there was a virtual safety car to recover Lance Stroll's stricken Aston Martin, and pitting under the safety car at this track and, with a very high speed straight passing the 50mph pit-lane zone, this saves nine seconds on the normal 24 seconds lost when everyone is otherwise at full speed out on track.

Russell was leading on the hard tyres and he wasn't called in. Right behind him his team-mate Antonelli and rival Verstappen did pit to shed their used medium-compound tyres. Russell said in the post-race interviews that he thought both cars were staying out. In the team press release he's quoted very diplomatically as saying the team split strategies as it was not clear whether track advantage ahead of all traffic was the right way to go, or taking on fresh tyres. My guess is he's feeling bruised by how that played out.

Antonelli set about the task of catching up the 15 seconds lost, including passing people like Norris and Hamilton, and once again he made impressive progress. Verstappen became embroiled in a battle with both McLarens, including the feisty Piastri and so it became effectively an all silver two-horse race. Game on.

Antonelli was catching at sometimes over one second per lap on his fresh tyres and passed traffic relatively easily. As he coasted up to the back of Russell for the second time that afternoon the pass seemed inevitable. Russell wasn't going to make it easy, braking very late into the first chicane, running slightly wide. Antonelli would drift wide in the left-hander immediately following and would also find loose stones from a surface which was breaking up.

The asphalt had been repaired Friday evening but after many races and much of the grand prix, it was failing again. Antonelli found himself far into the gravel but recovered to the racetrack still ahead of Verstappen. He had some catching up to do again which he quickly achieved. Heading up to Ascari chicane Russell hung left and Antonelli was through once more, to rapturous cheers from the crowd.

Both drivers had been asked to race clean, Russell even being told to 'bring it home'. Did Russell let Antonelli through hoping to pick up the overtake mode heading into the last corner? His tyres were 50 laps old by the chequered flag and in reality he was out of any credible options.

An Italian won the Italian Grand Prix for the first time in 60 years, and the crowd weren't going to waste the moment, it was electric.

The best duel at the finish was between the two McLarens of Piastri and Norris. Piastri had been less than motivated to give Norris a slipstream in qualifying, to say the least judging by a few factors, and Norris felt that Piastri had him on the grass at high speed heading towards the second chicane in the closing stages, although there wasn't much room to start with in reality.

Norris went over the first chicane on the final lap, which ironically may have helped him with energy deployment on the last lap, and he squeezed past the young Aussie to finish a mere two tenths of a second ahead. That all looked a bit personal.

The Theatre of Speed perhaps needs renaming the Theatre of Overtaking in this era of F1, but it was breathless to watch. Now we head to Madrid and a track which looks like it could be challenging for other reasons.
